translations.idiomatic: Monthly grain cannot stop overnight. Willing tenants should receive land by head count at once.

sentences.zh: 自餘僻遠不願者，宜准近制，系官荒地許軍民耕辟例，令軍民得占蒔之。

translations.literal: For the rest, remote and unwilling, the recent regulation allowing soldiers and civilians to open idle government wasteland should be followed, letting soldiers and civilians occupy and plant it.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest—remote families who refuse—apply the recent rule on opening idle government wasteland and let soldier and civilian alike claim and sow it.

sentences.zh: 」院官曰：「牧馬地少，且久荒難耕，軍戶複乏農器，然不給之，則彼自支糧外，更無從得食，非蓄銳待敵之計。

translations.literal: Court officials said: "Horse pasture is scarce, long wasteland is hard to farm, and military households also lack farming tools; yet if land is not granted, beyond their grain allowance they have no other means of food—not a plan for sharpening troops to await the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Court officials countered: "Pasture is thin, wasteland stubborn, tools scarce—yet deny them land and apart from rations they have nothing to eat. That is no way to keep an army sharp for battle."

sentences.zh: 給之則亦未能遽減其糧，若得遲以歲月，俟頗成倫次，漸可以省官廩耳。

translations.literal: If granted, grain cannot immediately be reduced; if time is allowed to pass in months and years, until things are fairly in order, official granary expenses can gradually be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Grant land and you still cannot cut rations tomorrow—but given years, once fields take shape, state granaries might slowly breathe easier.

sentences.zh: 今奪於有力者，即以授其無力者，恐無以耕。

translations.literal: Now if it is seized from the powerful and immediately given to the powerless, I fear there will be no means to farm.
translations.idiomatic: Snatch from the strong and hand to the weak, and I doubt anyone will plow it.

sentences.zh: 乞令司縣官勸率民戶，借牛破荒，至來春然後給之。

translations.literal: We request that county officials be ordered to encourage and lead households to lend oxen and break the wasteland; only in the coming spring should it be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Order local magistrates to rally peasants, lend oxen, break ground—and grant title only next spring.

sentences.zh: 司縣官能率民戶以助耕而無騷動者，量加官賞，庶幾有所激勸。

translations.literal: County officials who can lead households to assist cultivation without disturbance should receive measured official rewards, so that there may be some incentive.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who mobilize help without unrest deserve graded rewards—perhaps that would stir them to act.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣複曰：「若如所言，則司縣官貪慕官賞，必將抑配，以至擾民。

translations.literal: The councilors again said: "If it is as stated, county officials, greedy for official reward, will surely force allocations, until the people are disturbed."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers rejoined: "Reward hungry officials and they will force quotas on peasants until the countryside boils."

sentences.zh: 今民家之牛，量地而畜之。

translations.literal: Now civilian households' oxen are kept according to the measure of their land.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers keep only as many oxen as their own acreage requires.

sentences.zh: 況比年以來，農功甫畢則並力轉輸猶恐不及，豈有暇耕它人之田也。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent years, as soon as the harvest is finished, joint transport still fears being insufficient—how could there be leisure to farm another person's fields?"
translations.idiomatic: These past years, harvest barely ends before every hand turns to convoy duty—who has time to break someone else's field?

sentences.zh: 惟如臣等前奏為便。

translations.literal: Only our previous memorial is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Our earlier proposal remains the better path.

sentences.zh: 」詔再議之。

translations.literal: A decree ordered further deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered another round of debate.

sentences.zh: 乃擬民有能開牧馬地及官荒地作熟田者，以半給之為永業，半給軍戶。

translations.literal: It was then proposed that civilians who can open horse pasture and government wasteland into fertile fields should receive half as permanent property and half for military households.
translations.idiomatic: They settled on a compromise: peasants who bring pasture and wasteland under the plow would keep half in perpetuity; half would pass to garrison households.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 四年，省奏：「自古用兵，且耕且戰，是以兵食交足。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Ministry memorialized: "Since antiquity in employing armies, one both farms and fights; thus military provisions and food mutually suffice."
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Ministry recalled the old principle: "Armies that farm while they fight never run short of grain."

sentences.zh: 今諸帥分兵不啻百萬，一充軍伍咸仰於官，至於婦子居家安坐待哺，蓋不知屯田為經久之計也。

translations.literal: Now the various commanders' dispersed troops are no less than a million; once enrolled in the ranks all depend on the state; as for wives and children who stay home sitting at ease awaiting rations—they plainly do not know that garrison farming is the long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: Today the field armies number well over a million men, every soldier in the ranks fed from the public granaries, while wives and children sit idle at home waiting to be fed—they seem to have forgotten that colony fields are the only enduring solution.

sentences.zh: 願下明詔，令諸帥府各以其軍耕耨，亦以逸待勞之策也。

translations.literal: We pray that Your Majesty issue a clear edict ordering each command headquarters to have its army plow and weed; it is also the strategy of meeting fatigue with rest.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to proclaim clearly that every command should put its troops to the plow—rest the army while wearing down the land.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 興定三年正月，尚書右丞領三司事侯摯言：「按河南軍民田總一百九十七萬頃有奇，見耕種者九十六萬餘頃，上田可收一石二斗，中田一石，下田八斗，十一取之，歲得九百六十萬石，自可優給歲支，且使貧富均，大小各得其所。

translations.literal: In the first month of Xingding 3, Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat and Commissioner of the Three Offices Hou Zhi said: "According to our survey, military and civilian fields in Henan total 1,970,000-odd qing; those presently under cultivation exceed 960,000 qing. Upper-grade land yields one shi two dou, middle grade one shi, lower grade eight dou; taking one in eleven, the annual harvest reaches 9,600,000 shi—enough to amply cover yearly expenditures, and to equalize rich and poor so that great and small each find their place.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xingding 3, Hou Zhi, Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat and head of the Three Offices, reported: "Henan holds nearly two million qing of military and civilian land, of which more than nine hundred sixty thousand qing are under the plow. Top fields yield one shi two dou, middling fields one shi, poor fields eight dou; assessed at one part in eleven, the yearly harvest comes to nine million six hundred thousand shi—enough to meet annual needs in full, and to let rich and poor, great and small, each take a fair share.

sentences.zh: 臣在東平嘗試行二三年，民不疲而軍用足。

translations.literal: When I tried this in Dongping for two or three years, the people were not exhausted and military supplies were ample.
translations.idiomatic: I trial-tested the policy in Dongping for two or three years: the peasants did not buckle, and the army never wanted for grain.

sentences.zh: 」詔有司議行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the responsible offices to deliberate and implement it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne referred the proposal to the responsible offices for deliberation and execution.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，移剌不言：「軍戶自徙于河南，數歲尚未給田，兼以移徙不常，莫得安居，故貧者甚眾。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year, Yelü Buyan said: "Since military households were relocated to Henan, for several years land has still not been allotted; coupled with frequent moves, they cannot settle in peace, hence the poor are extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year four, Yelü Buyan said: "Garrison households were moved to Henan years ago, yet many still have no land. They are shunted from post to post and cannot put down roots; no wonder poverty runs so deep.

sentences.zh: 請括諸屯處官田，人給三十畝，仍不移屯它所，如此則軍戶可以得所，官糧可以漸省。

translations.literal: We request that government fields at all garrison sites be registered and thirty mu apiece granted, without relocating the garrison elsewhere; thus military households can find their footing and state grain rations can gradually be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Register the government fields at every garrison and grant thirty mu per man, without shifting the camps elsewhere. The soldiers would finally have a livelihood, and the state ration rolls could slowly shrink.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣奏：「前此亦有言授地者，樞密院以謂俟事緩而行之。

translations.literal: The ministers memorialized: "Previously too there were proposals to grant land; the Bureau of Military Affairs held that it should wait until affairs eased.
translations.idiomatic: The council replied: "Land grants have been proposed before. The Bureau of Military Affairs said to wait until the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 今河南罹水災，流亡者眾，所種麥不及五萬頃，殆減往年太半，歲所入殆不能足。

translations.literal: Now Henan has suffered flood, refugees are many, wheat sown falls short of 50,000 qing—nearly half last year's area—and annual revenue scarcely suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Henan has just been drowned; refugees crowd the roads. Wheat plantings fall short of fifty thousand qing—nearly half last year's acreage—and this year's intake will barely cover expenses.

sentences.zh: 若撥授之為永業，俟有獲即罷其家糧，亦省費之一端也。

translations.literal: If allotments are granted as permanent holdings, once harvests come in their household rations can be abolished—it is also one means of saving expense.
translations.idiomatic: Grant the land as permanent holdings, and once they harvest, cut off the family rations—that alone would save a fortune.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又河南水災，逋戶太半，田野荒蕪，恐賦入少而國用乏，遂命唐、鄧、裕、察、息、壽、潁、亳及歸德府被水田，已燥者布種，未滲者種稻，複業之戶免本租及一切差發，能代耕者如之，有司擅科者以違制論，闕牛及食者率富者就貸。

translations.literal: Henan suffered flood again; absconding households exceeded half and fields lay waste. Fearing reduced revenue and strained state coffers, the court ordered waterlogged fields in Tang, Deng, Yu, Cha, Xi, Shou, Ying, Bo, and Guide Prefecture—where dry, to sow grain; where still sodden, to plant rice. Returning households were exempted from base rent and all corvée levies; those who could farm on others' behalf received the same. Officials who imposed unauthorized exactions were prosecuted for violation of regulations; those lacking oxen or food were directed to borrow from the wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Floods struck Henan again. More than half the registered households had fled, and the countryside lay fallow. Fearful that revenue would collapse and the treasury run dry, the court ordered the inundated districts of Tang, Deng, Yu, Cha, Xi, Shou, Ying, Bo, and Guide: where the soil had dried, sow grain; where water still stood, plant rice. Households returning to their farms were freed from base rent and every corvée levy, and those who tilled for others received the same relief. Unauthorized exactions by local officials were punished as violations of statute; peasants short of oxen or food were sent to borrow from the wealthy.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，京南行三司石抹斡魯言：「京南、東、西三路，屯軍老幼四十萬口，歲費糧百四十余萬石，皆坐食民租，甚非善計。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Shimo Walu of the Jingnan Branch Three Offices said: "On the Jingnan, Eastern, and Western circuits, garrison troops young and old number 400,000 mouths, consuming over 1,400,000 shi of grain yearly—all living off civilian rent. This is a poor plan indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year five, Shimo Walu of the Jingnan Branch Three Offices said: "On the Jingnan, Eastern, and Western routes, four hundred thousand garrison mouths, young and old, consume more than 1.4 million shi of grain each year—all of it drawn from civilian rent. There is no sound policy in this.

sentences.zh: 宜括逋戶舊耕田，南京一路舊墾田三十九萬八千五百餘頃，內官田民耕者九萬九千頃有奇。

translations.literal: Government fields formerly tilled by absconding households should be registered. On the Nanjing circuit alone, formerly opened land totals 398,500-odd qing; within this, government land farmed by civilians exceeds 99,000 qing.
translations.idiomatic: The old fields of fugitive households should be registered and reclaimed. On the Nanjing circuit alone, formerly cleared land comes to more than 398,500 qing; of that, civilians already farm nearly 100,000 qing of government soil.

sentences.zh: 今饑民流離者太半，東、西、南路計亦如之，朝廷雖招使複業，民恐既複之後生計未定而賦斂隨之，往往匿而不出。

translations.literal: Now starving folk in flight exceed half; the Eastern and Western southern routes are much the same. Though the court recruits them to resume farming, people fear that once they return their livelihood is unsettled while levies follow—they often hide and do not appear.
translations.idiomatic: More than half the hungry have scattered; the Eastern and Western southern routes fare no better. The court calls them home, but peasants fear that the moment they return, taxes will follow before their livelihood is secure—so they stay hidden.

sentences.zh: 若分給軍戶人三十畝，使之自耕，或召人佃種，可數歲之後畜積漸饒，官糧可罷。

translations.literal: If thirty mu apiece were granted to military households for self-cultivation, or tenant farmers recruited, within a few years stores would gradually grow ample and state rations could cease.
translations.idiomatic: Give each garrison household thirty mu to farm for itself, or lease the land to tenants, and within a few years the granaries would fill; then the state rations could end.

sentences.zh: 」令省臣議之，更不能行。

translations.literal: The order was referred to the provincial ministers for deliberation, but again it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the provincial ministers to debate the plan—and once again nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 金制，官地輸租，私田輸稅。

translations.literal: Under Jin institutions, government land paid rent; private fields paid tax.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin law, government land owed rent; private land owed tax.

sentences.zh: 租之制不傳，大率分田之等為九而差次之。

translations.literal: The rent system is not fully transmitted; generally field grades were divided into nine and assessed by rank.
translations.idiomatic: The rent code itself has not come down intact; in general, fields were ranked in nine grades and taxed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 夏稅畝取三合，秋稅畝取五升，又納秸一束，束十有五斤。

translations.literal: Summer tax took three he per mu; autumn tax five sheng per mu; also one bundle of stalks, fifteen jin per bundle.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax was three he per mu; autumn tax five sheng per mu, plus one bundle of straw weighing fifteen jin.

sentences.zh: 夏稅六月止八月，秋稅十月止十二月，為初、中、末三限，州三百裏外，紓其期一月。

translations.literal: Summer tax ran from the sixth month through the eighth, autumn from the tenth through the twelfth, in initial, middle, and final quotas; for prefectures beyond three hundred li, deadlines were extended one month.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax was due between the sixth and eighth months, autumn tax between the tenth and twelfth, each in three installments; prefectures more than three hundred li distant were granted an extra month.

sentences.zh: 屯田戶佃官地者，有司移猛安謀克督之。

translations.literal: For tuntian households renting government land, the responsible offices delegated supervision to the meng'an-mouke.
translations.idiomatic: Tuntian households farming government land were overseen by the local meng'an-mouke, as ordered by the civil authorities.

sentences.zh: 泰和五年，章宗諭宰臣曰：「十月民獲未畢，遽令納稅可乎？

translations.literal: In Taihe 5, Zhangzong told the ministers: "In the tenth month the people's harvest is not yet complete—can we rush them to pay tax?
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5, Emperor Zhangzong asked his ministers: "In the tenth month the harvest is still underway—is it right to demand tax payment so soon?

sentences.zh: 」改秋稅限十一月為初。

translations.literal: The initial deadline for autumn tax was changed to the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: The first autumn-tax installment was moved to the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 中都、西京、北京、上京、遼東、臨潢、陝西地寒，稼穡遲熟，夏稅限以七月為初。

translations.literal: Zhongdu, the Western Capital, Northern Capital, Upper Capital, Liaodong, Linhuang, and Shaanxi—cold regions where crops ripen late—set the initial summer-tax deadline to the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: In the cold northern circuits—Zhongdu, Western Capital, Northern Capital, Upper Capital, Liaodong, Linhuang, and Shaanxi—where grain ripens late, the first summer-tax deadline was set to the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 凡輸送粟麥，三百裏外石減五升，以上每三百里遞減五升。

translations.literal: For transporting grain, beyond three hundred li five sheng were deducted per shi; above that, five sheng less for each further three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: For grain deliveries, five sheng per shi was forgiven beyond three hundred li, and another five sheng per shi for every additional three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 粟折秸百稱者，百里內減三稱，二百里減五稱，不及三百里減八稱，三百里及輸本色槁草，各減十稱。

translations.literal: For grain commuted to stalks at one hundred cheng: within one hundred li, three cheng were deducted; at two hundred li, five; under three hundred li, eight; at three hundred li and for payment in straw in kind, ten cheng each.
translations.idiomatic: When grain was commuted to straw at one hundred cheng per unit, carriers within one hundred li were forgiven three cheng, at two hundred li five cheng, under three hundred li eight cheng; at three hundred li, or when paying straw in kind, ten cheng were forgiven in each case.

sentences.zh: 計民田園、邸舍、車乘、牧畜、種植之資，藏鏹之數，征錢有差，謂之物力錢。

translations.literal: Households' gardens, townhouses, vehicles, livestock, planted assets, and stores of cash were counted and money levied in varying amounts—called wuli cash.
translations.idiomatic: The state tallied each household's gardens, townhouses, carts, livestock, plantings, and hoarded coin, and levied cash in graded amounts—this was called the wuli levy.

sentences.zh: 遇差科，必按版籍，先及富者，勢均則以丁多寡定甲乙。

translations.literal: When corvée levies arose, registers were consulted and the wealthy were reached first; where standing was equal, priority grades were set by number of adult males.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever special corvée was imposed, officials checked the household registers, called on the wealthy first, and where wealth was equal, ranked households by the number of adult males.

sentences.zh: 有橫科，則視物力，循大至小均科。

translations.literal: For emergency levies, wuli was considered and assessments spread from great to small.
translations.idiomatic: For emergency exactions, officials looked to each household's wuli assessment and spread the burden from the richest down.

sentences.zh: 其或不可分摘者，率以次戶濟之。

translations.literal: Where burdens could not be separately assigned, lower-grade households were generally tapped to cover the gap.
translations.idiomatic: When a levy could not be divided precisely, the shortfall was usually made up from the next lower grade of households.

sentences.zh: 凡民之物力，所居之宅不預。

translations.literal: In calculating civilian wuli, the dwelling itself was not included.
translations.idiomatic: In assessing civilian wuli, the home one lived in was excluded.

sentences.zh: 猛安謀克戶、監戶、官戶所居外，自置民田宅，則預其數。

translations.literal: Apart from the dwellings of meng'an-mouke, prison, and official households, privately held civilian fields and homes were counted.
translations.idiomatic: Only the residence of a meng'an-mouke, prison, or official household was exempt; any private civilian land or dwelling they owned elsewhere was counted.

sentences.zh: 墓田、學田，租稅、物力皆免。

translations.literal: Grave fields and school fields were exempt from rent, tax, and wuli.
translations.idiomatic: Grave plots and school lands owed no rent, no tax, and no wuli levy.

sentences.zh: 民訴水旱應免者，河南、山東、河東、大名、京兆、鳳翔、彰德部內支郡，夏田四月，秋田七月，余路夏以五月，秋以八月，水田則通以八月為限，遇閏月則展期半月，限外訴者不理。

translations.literal: For civilian petitions seeking flood or drought relief: in branch counties of Henan, Shandong, Hedong, Daming, Jingzhao, Fengxiang, and Zhangde, summer crops by the fourth month and autumn crops by the seventh; on other circuits, summer by the fifth month and autumn by the eighth; paddy fields uniformly by the eighth month. An intercalary month extended the deadline half a month; petitions after the deadline were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants claiming flood or drought relief had to petition by fixed deadlines: in the branch counties of Henan, Shandong, Hedong, Daming, Jingzhao, Fengxiang, and Zhangde, by the fourth month for summer crops and the seventh for autumn; elsewhere by the fifth month for summer and the eighth for autumn; paddy fields in all circuits by the eighth month. An intercalary month added half a month; late petitions were rejected.

sentences.zh: 非時之災則無限。

translations.literal: For untimely disasters there was no deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters that struck out of season carried no time limit.

sentences.zh: 損十之八者全免，七分免所損之數，六分則全征。

translations.literal: Loss of eight-tenths brought full exemption; seven-tenths, exemption of the amount lost; six-tenths, full levy.
translations.idiomatic: If eight parts in ten were lost, tax was remitted entirely; if seven, remission matched the loss; if six, the full levy stood.

sentences.zh: 桑被災不能蠶，則免絲綿絹稅。

translations.literal: If mulberry was disaster-struck and silkworms could not be raised, silk, cotton, and cloth taxes were waived.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster ruined the mulberry and silkworms could not be raised, taxes in silk, cotton, and cloth were waived.

sentences.zh: 諸路雨雪及禾稼收穫之數，月以捷步申戶部。

translations.literal: Each circuit's figures for rain, snow, and harvest were reported monthly to the Ministry of Revenue by courier.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit sent monthly courier reports to the Ministry of Revenue on rain, snow, and harvest totals.

sentences.zh: 凡敘使品官之家，並免雜役，驗物力所當輸者、止出雇錢。

translations.literal: Households of ranked officials by appointment were exempt from miscellaneous corvée; verified wuli obligations required only substitution cash.
translations.idiomatic: Families of appointed officials of rank were freed from miscellaneous corvée; where wuli obligations remained, they paid hire-money in lieu of labor.

sentences.zh: 進納補官未至廕子孫、及凡有出身者、謂司吏、譯人等。

translations.literal: Those who bought office but had not yet reached status to ennoble descendants, and all with formal entry—meaning clerks, translators, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: This covered men who had purchased office but not yet earned hereditary rank for their sons, and all who held formal entry—clerks, translators, and the like.

sentences.zh: 出職帶官敘當身者、雜班敘使五品以下、及正品承應已帶散官未出職者，子孫與其同居兄弟，下逮終場舉人，系籍學生、醫學生，皆免一身之役。

translations.literal: Those who had left office but retained nominal rank for their person; miscellaneous-sequence envoys of fifth rank and below; proper-grade attendants who already held scattered rank but had not yet left office—their descendants and co-resident brothers, down to examination graduates at the final session, registered students, and medical students—were all exempt from personal corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Also exempt were men who had retired but still carried nominal rank; miscellaneous envoys of fifth rank and below; attendants of regular grade who held scattered rank but had not yet taken formal leave—their sons and brothers living under the same roof, down to final-session examination graduates, registered students, and medical students—all were freed from personal corvée.

sentences.zh: 三代同居，已旌門則免差發，三年後免雜役。

translations.literal: Three generations living together: if the gate had been honored, corvée dispatch was waived; after three years, miscellaneous corvée was waived.
translations.idiomatic: Where three generations dwelt together and the family gate had been honored by imperial commendation, corvée dispatch was waived at once and all miscellaneous corvée after three years.

sentences.zh: 太宗天會元年，敕有司輕徭賦，勸稼穡。

translations.literal: Taizong, Tianhui 1: ordered the offices to lighten corvée and levies and encourage agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 1, Emperor Taizong ordered the offices to ease corvée and taxes and to encourage farming.

sentences.zh: 十年，以遼人士庶之族賦役等差不一，詔有司命悉均之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, because Khitan elite and commoners had uneven corvée grades, an edict ordered the offices to equalize them entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten, because corvée fell unevenly on Khitan nobles and commoners alike, the throne commanded that all distinctions be leveled.

sentences.zh: 熙宗天眷五年十二月，詔免民戶殘欠租稅。

translations.literal: Xizong, twelfth month of Tianjuan 5: an edict remitted households' arrears of rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tianjuan 5, Emperor Xizong remitted outstanding rent and tax owed by civilian households.

sentences.zh: 皇統三年，蠲民稅之未足者。

translations.literal: Huangtong 3: remitted unpaid civilian taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 3, unpaid civilian taxes were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定二年五月，謂宰臣曰：「凡有徭役，均科強戶，不得抑配貧民。

translations.literal: Shizong, fifth month of Dading 2, told the ministers: "Whenever corvée arises, levy evenly on strong households—do not force allocation onto the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Dading 2, Emperor Shizong told his ministers: "Whenever corvée is imposed, spread it across the strong households—never force the burden onto the poor.

sentences.zh: 」有言以用度不足，奏預借河北東西路、中都租稅，上以國用雖乏，民力尤艱，遂不允。

translations.literal: Someone argued that expenditures were insufficient and memorialized to advance-borrow rent and tax from the Hebei Eastern and Western circuits and Zhongdu; the emperor held that though state coffers were strained, popular strength was yet more grievous—and refused.
translations.idiomatic: When officials cited empty coffers and proposed advancing rent and tax from the Hebei Eastern and Western circuits and Zhongdu, the emperor replied that though the treasury was bare, the people's strength was far more exhausted—and he refused.

sentences.zh: 三年，以歲歉，詔免二年租稅。

translations.literal: In the third year, because the year's harvest was poor, an edict remitted two years' rent and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, harvests failed, and the throne ordered a two-year remission of rent and taxes.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「朕比以元帥府從宜行事，今聞河南、陝西、山東、北京以東、及北邊州郡，調發甚多，而省部又與他州一例征取賦役，是重擾也。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "I recently permitted the Marshal's Office to act as circumstances required. Now I hear that in Henan, Shaanxi, Shandong, the region east of the Beijing circuit, and the northern frontier prefectures and districts, deployments are very numerous, yet the provincial and central ministries likewise levy land tax and corvée from them on the same terms as other circuits—this is double harassment."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "I had lately allowed the Marshal's Headquarters to act at discretion. Now word reaches me that Henan, Shaanxi, Shandong, the country east of the Beijing circuit, and the northern frontier districts are being levied for war deployments far beyond their capacity—yet the ministries still collect the same levies and corvée as every other circuit. The people are being harassed twice over."

sentences.zh: 可憑元帥府已取者例，蠲除之。

translations.literal: One may rely on precedents set by what the Marshal's Office has already taken, and remit the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the Marshal's Office has already collected should serve as precedent; the rest is to be remitted.

sentences.zh: 」五年，命有司：「凡罹蝗旱水溢之地，蠲其賦稅。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year, [the emperor] ordered the responsible offices: "All lands that have suffered locusts, drought, or flooding—remit their levies and taxes."
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year he directed the responsible offices: "Wherever locusts, drought, or flood have struck, remit all levies and taxes there."

sentences.zh: 」六年，以河北、山東水，免其租。

translations.literal: " In the sixth year, because of flooding in Hebei and Shandong, their rent was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth year, floods in Hebei and Shandong brought a remission of rent.

sentences.zh: 八年十月，彰德軍節度使高昌福上書言稅租甚重，上諭翰林學士張景仁曰：「今租稅法比近代甚輕，而以為重，何也？

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year, Gao Changfu, Military Commissioner of the Zhangde Army, submitted a memorial saying rent and taxes were very heavy. The emperor instructed Hanlin Academician Zhang Jingren: "Present rent-and-tax law is quite light compared with recent times—so why do they consider it heavy?"
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighth year, Zhangde's military commissioner Gao Changfu memorialized that rent and taxes were crushingly heavy. The emperor told Hanlin academician Zhang Jingren: "Our tax laws are lighter than anything in recent memory—so why does he call them heavy?"

sentences.zh: 」景仁曰：「今之稅斂殊輕，非稅斂則國用何從而出？

translations.literal: " Jingren said: "Today's tax levies are extraordinarily light. Without tax levies, whence would state expenditure come?"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang replied: "Tax collection today is remarkably light. Without it, where would state revenue come from?"

sentences.zh: 」二年二月，尚書省奏：「天下倉廩貯粟二千七十九萬余石。

translations.literal: " In the second month of the second year, the Ministry of State Affairs memorialized: "Granaries throughout the realm store grain exceeding twenty million, seven hundred and ninety thousand shi."
translations.idiomatic: " In the second month of the second year, the Ministry reported: "Realm-wide granaries hold more than 20.79 million shi of grain."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕聞國無九年之蓄則國非其國，朕是以括天下之田以均其賦，歲取九百萬石，自經費七百萬石外，二百萬石又為水旱之所蠲免及賑貸之用，余才百萬石而已。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I have heard that if a state lacks a nine-year store, it is not truly a state. Therefore I surveyed all land under heaven to equalize levies, taking nine million shi annually. Apart from seven million shi for regular expenditure, two million shi go toward remissions for flood and drought and for relief loans; barely one million shi remain."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "A realm without a nine-year grain reserve is no realm at all. That is why I surveyed the empire's fields and equalized the levy, collecting nine million shi each year. Seven million cover ordinary expenditure; two million go to drought and flood remissions and relief loans. Barely a million remain in reserve."

sentences.zh: 朕廣蓄積，備饑謹也。

translations.literal: I broaden stores and accumulation to guard against famine.
translations.idiomatic: I am building reserves against famine—that is the point.

sentences.zh: 小民以為稅重，小臣沽民譽，亦多議之。

translations.literal: Ordinary people consider taxes heavy; minor officials buy popular acclaim, and many also criticize [them].
translations.idiomatic: Common folk call the taxes heavy; petty officials court popularity, and many join the chorus of complaint.

sentences.zh: 蓋不慮國家緩急之備也。」

translations.literal: They simply do not weigh the state's provisions for urgency and emergency."
translations.idiomatic: They spare no thought for what the state must hold in reserve for crisis."

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，以水旱免中都、西京、南京、河北、河東、山東、陝西去年租稅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, because of flood and drought, the previous year's rent and taxes were remitted in Zhongdu, Western Capital, Southern Capital, Hebei, Hedong, Shandong, and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year, flood and drought brought a remission of the previous year's rent and taxes in Zhongdu, the Western and Southern Capitals, Hebei, Hedong, Shandong, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十三年，謂宰臣曰：「民間科差，計所免已過半矣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he told the chief ministers: "Among civilian corvée and levies, those already remitted account for more than half by estimate."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, he told his chief ministers: "By my reckoning, more than half of the corvée and levies owed by commoners have already been remitted."

sentences.zh: 慮小民不能詳知，吏緣為奸，仍舊征取，其令所在揭榜諭之。

translations.literal: Fearing that common people could not know the details, and that clerks would seize the opportunity for corruption and continue collecting as before, he ordered that proclamations be posted locally to inform them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that ordinary people would not learn the details and that clerks would exploit the confusion to keep collecting as before, he ordered notices posted everywhere to make the remissions plain.

sentences.zh: 」十月，敕州縣官不盡力催督稅租，以致逋懸者，可止其俸，使之征足，然後給之。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month, he commanded that prefectural and district officials who failed to exert themselves in pressing for rent and tax collection, causing unpaid arrears, should have their salaries withheld until collection was complete—only then would salaries be paid.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month he ordered that any prefectural or district official who failed to press hard for rent and tax, allowing arrears to pile up, should have his salary stopped until the shortfall was made up—only then would he be paid again.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，詔免去年被水旱路分租稅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year, an edict remitted the previous year's rent and taxes for circuit subdivisions stricken by flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year, an edict remitted the previous year's rent and taxes in every circuit subdivision hit by flood or drought.

sentences.zh: 十七年，上問宰臣曰：「遼東賦稅舊六萬余石，通檢後幾二十萬。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the emperor asked the chief ministers: "Liaodong's land-tax levy formerly ran to a little over sixty thousand shi; after the comprehensive survey it approaches two hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, the emperor asked his chief ministers: "Liaodong's land tax once yielded a little over sixty thousand shi; after the comprehensive survey it nears two hundred thousand."

sentences.zh: 六萬時何以仰給，二十萬後所積幾何？

translations.literal: When it was sixty thousand, how were expenses met? After two hundred thousand, how much accumulates?"
translations.idiomatic: When the levy was sixty thousand shi, how did the circuit meet its costs? Now that it is two hundred thousand, how much is actually saved?"

sentences.zh: 」戶部契勘，謂：「先以官吏數少故能給，今官吏兵卒及孤老數多，以此費大。

translations.literal: " The Ministry of Revenue verified and replied: "Formerly there were few officials and clerks, so supplies sufficed; now officials, soldiers, and the widowed and elderly are far more numerous, hence expenses are great."
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry of Revenue investigated and answered: "Before, there were few officials and clerks, so the revenue was enough; now there are far more officials, soldiers, and widowed and elderly dependents, and costs have risen accordingly."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「當察其實，毋令妄費也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Investigate the facts, and do not allow wasteful spending."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Look into the truth of the matter, and do not permit reckless spending."

sentences.zh: 」十七年三月，詔免河北、山東、陝西、河東、西京、遼東等十路去年被旱蝗租稅。

translations.literal: " In the third month of the seventeenth year, an edict remitted the previous year's rent and taxes for the ten circuits of Hebei, Shandong, Shaanxi, Hedong, Western Capital, Liaodong, and others, stricken by drought and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month of the seventeenth year, an edict remitted the previous year's rent and taxes in ten circuits—Hebei, Shandong, Shaanxi, Hedong, the Western Capital, Liaodong, and the rest—where drought and locusts had struck.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighteenth year,

sentences.zh: 免中都、河北、河東、山東、河南、陝西等路前年被災租稅。

translations.literal: Rent and taxes were remitted for the previous year's disaster in the circuits of Zhongdu, Hebei, Hedong, Shandong, Henan, Shaanxi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: rent and taxes were remitted for the previous year's disaster in Zhongdu, Hebei, Hedong, Shandong, Henan, Shaanxi, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 十九年秋，中都、西京、河北、山東、河東、陝西以水旱傷民田十三萬七千七百餘頃，詔蠲其租。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the nineteenth year, flood and drought damaged 137,700-plus qing of civilian fields in Zhongdu, Western Capital, Hebei, Shandong, Hedong, and Shaanxi; an edict remitted their rent.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the nineteenth year, flood and drought ruined more than 137,700 qing of civilian farmland in Zhongdu, the Western Capital, Hebei, Shandong, Hedong, and Shaanxi; an edict remitted the rent on those fields.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，以中都、西京、河北、山東、河東、陝西路前歲被災，詔免其租稅。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year, because the circuits of Zhongdu, Western Capital, Hebei, Shandong, Hedong, and Shaanxi had suffered disaster the previous year, an edict remitted their rent and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twentieth year, because Zhongdu, the Western Capital, Hebei, Shandong, Hedong, and Shaanxi had been disaster-stricken the year before, an edict remitted their rent and taxes.

sentences.zh: 以戶部尚書曹望之之言，詔減鄜延及河東南路稅五十二萬余石，增河北西路稅八萬八千石。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Cao Wangzhi, Minister of Revenue, an edict reduced taxes in Fuyan and Hedong South Circuit by over 520,000 shi and increased taxes in Hebei West Circuit by 88,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on the advice of Minister of Revenue Cao Wangzhi, the throne ordered taxes in Fuyan and Hedong South Circuit cut by more than 520,000 shi and taxes in Hebei West Circuit raised by 88,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 又詔諸稅粟非關邊要之地者，除當儲數外，聽民從便折納。

translations.literal: Another edict [said]: for tax grain in regions not critical to the frontier, beyond what must be stored, civilians were permitted to commute payment as they saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared that in regions not vital to the frontier, once storage quotas were met, civilians might commute their grain tax in whatever form suited them.

sentences.zh: 二十一年九月，以中都水災，免租。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-first year, because of flooding in Zhongdu, rent was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-first year, flooding in Zhongdu brought a remission of rent.

sentences.zh: 前時近官路百姓以牛夫充遞運者，複於它處未嘗就役之家征錢償之。

translations.literal: Previously, when commoners near the official roads supplied ox-drivers for relay transport, money was also levied from households elsewhere that had not served, to compensate them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when commoners living near the imperial highways supplied ox-drivers for relay transport, the state also collected cash from households elsewhere that had not served, to pay them compensation.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，宗州民王仲規告乞征還所役牛夫錢，省臣以奏，上曰：「此既就役，複征錢於彼，前雖如此行之，複恐所給錢未必能到本戶，是兩不便也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Wang Zhonggui, a civilian of Zong Prefecture, petitioned to recover money paid for ox-driver corvée. The provincial ministers memorialized, and the emperor said: "Those here have already served—yet money is levied again from those there. Though this was done before, I fear the money paid out may not reach the household that actually served. Both sides suffer."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, Wang Zhonggui, a commoner of Zong Prefecture, petitioned for repayment of the cash levied for ox-driver corvée. The provincial ministers reported the case, and the emperor said: "The households that served are charged again, while money is collected from others who did not. This practice has stood for some time, but I doubt the compensation ever reaches the household that actually bore the labor. Nobody is well served."

sentences.zh: 不若止計所役，免租稅及鋪馬錢為便。

translations.literal: Better simply to count who has served and remit their rent, taxes, and relay-horse fees.
translations.idiomatic: Better simply to tally who has served and remit their rent, taxes, and relay-horse fees in lieu of cash.

sentences.zh: 其預計實數以聞。

translations.literal: Estimate the actual figures and report.
translations.idiomatic: Work out the actual numbers and report them.

sentences.zh: 若和雇價直亦須裁定也。

translations.literal: If hired-labor rates apply, those too must be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: If hired-labor rates are involved, those must be fixed as well.

sentences.zh: 」有司上其數，歲約給六萬四千余貫，計折粟八萬六千余石。

translations.literal: " The responsible offices submitted figures: annual payment would run to a little over 64,000 strings of cash, reckoned as a grain commutation of over 86,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: " The responsible offices submitted their figures: annual outlay would come to a little over 64,000 strings of cash, equivalent to more than 86,000 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 上複命，自今役牛夫之家，以去道三十裏內居者充役。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered further: from now on, households supplying ox-drivers for corvée must be those dwelling within thirty li of the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added a further order: henceforth only households living within thirty li of the highway might be pressed for ox-driver corvée.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，軍民地罹水旱之災者，二十一萬頃免稅凡四十九萬余石。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, military and civilian lands stricken by flood and drought—210,000 qing—received tax remissions totaling over 490,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, 210,000 qing of military and civilian land hit by flood and drought received tax remissions totaling more than 490,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 二十七年六月，免中都、河北等路嘗被河決水災軍民租稅。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-seventh year, rent and taxes were remitted for military and civilian households in Zhongdu, Hebei, and other circuits previously struck by river-breach flooding.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-seventh year, rent and taxes were remitted for military and civilian households in Zhongdu, Hebei, and other circuits that had earlier suffered river-breach floods.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔河水泛溢，農田被災者，與免差稅一年。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict [said]: where river waters overflowed and farmland suffered disaster, grant a one-year remission of corvée and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, an edict granted a one-year remission of corvée and taxes wherever river floods had ruined farmland.

sentences.zh: 懷、衛、孟、鄭四州塞河勞役，並免今年差稅。

translations.literal: The four prefectures of Huai, Wei, Meng, and Zheng, worn by labor to block the river, were all granted remission of this year's corvée and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The four prefectures of Huai, Wei, Meng, and Zheng, exhausted by labor to stem the river, were all granted remission of this year's corvée and taxes.

sentences.zh: 章宗大定二十九年，赦民租十之一。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhangzong, in the twenty-ninth year of Dading, the amnesty remitted one-tenth of civilian rent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading, under Emperor Zhangzong, an amnesty remitted one-tenth of civilian rent.

sentences.zh: 河東南北路則量減之。

translations.literal: In Hedong North and South Circuits it was reduced proportionally.
translations.idiomatic: In Hedong North and South Circuits the remission was scaled to local conditions.

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏，兩路田多峻阪，磽瘠者往往再歲一易，若不以地等級蠲除，則有不均。

translations.literal: The Ministry memorialized that in the two circuits much land lay on steep slopes; barren fields were often rotated every two years—if remissions did not follow land grades, the burden would be uneven.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry reported that in those two circuits much land climbed steep slopes and poor fields were often left fallow every other year; unless remissions followed land grades, the relief would fall unevenly.

sentences.zh: 遂敕以赦書特免一分外，中田複減一分，下田減二分。

translations.literal: They were commanded that beyond the one-tenth specially remitted by the amnesty edict, middle-grade fields received an additional one-tenth reduction and lower-grade fields a two-tenths reduction.
translations.idiomatic: An order followed: beyond the one-tenth amnesty remission, middle-grade fields received an additional one-tenth cut and lower-grade fields a two-tenths cut.

sentences.zh: 舊制，夏、秋稅納麥、粟、草三色，以各處所須之物不一，戶部複令以諸所用物折納。

translations.literal: Under the old system, summer and autumn taxes were paid in wheat, millet, and fodder grass in three kinds. Because required goods varied by locality, the Ministry of Revenue again ordered commutation in various goods as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, summer and autumn taxes were paid in wheat, millet, and fodder grass. Because each region required different goods, the Ministry of Revenue again ordered taxpayers to commute payment in whatever articles were needed locally.

sentences.zh: 上封事者言其不可，戶部謂如此則諸路所須之物要當和市，轉擾民矣。

translations.literal: A sealed memorial argued this was unworkable; the Ministry said that if so, each circuit would have to purchase required goods on the market, disturbing the people all the more.
translations.idiomatic: A sealed memorial to the throne argued that this would not do; the Ministry replied that without commutation, every circuit would have to buy what it needed on the market, harassing the people all the more.

sentences.zh: 遂命太府監，應折納之物為祗承宮禁者，治黃河薪芻增直二錢折納，如黃河岸所用木石固非土產，乃令所屬計置，而罷它應折納者。

translations.literal: They then ordered the Imperial Household Store: goods required for palace service and Yellow River firewood and fodder could be commuted with a two-cash premium; timber and stone used on the Yellow River bank were not local products, so subordinate offices were to procure them—and all other commutation requirements were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then ordered the Imperial Household Store to accept commutation, at a two-cash premium, for goods serving the palace and for Yellow River firewood and fodder; timber and stone used on the riverbank, not being local products, were to be procured by the offices concerned—and all other commutation requirements were abolished.

sentences.zh: 十一月，尚書省奏：「河南荒閑官地，許人計丁請佃，願仍為官者免租八年，願為己業者免稅三年。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Ministry memorialized: "Idle government wasteland in Henan may be rented by counting household members; those who wish to remain on government land receive eight years' rent remission; those who wish it as private holdings receive three years' tax remission."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the Ministry reported: "Idle government wasteland in Henan may be leased by counting adult males in the household; those who keep the land as government property receive eight years' rent remission, and those who take it as private holdings receive three years' tax remission."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年二月，敕自今民有訴水旱災傷者，即委官按視其實，申所屬州府，移報提刑司，同所屬檢畢，始令翻耕。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Mingchang, he commanded that from now on, when civilians petitioned for flood, drought, or disaster damage, officials should immediately be dispatched to verify the facts, report to the subordinate prefecture or circuit, notify the Judicial Intendant office, and only after inspection with the local authorities was complete might plowing resume be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Mingchang, he ordered that whenever commoners petitioned over flood, drought, or crop damage, officials should at once be sent to verify the facts, report to the prefecture or circuit concerned, notify the Judicial Intendant, and only after a joint inspection with local authorities was complete might the fields be cleared for replowing.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，有司言河州災傷，闕食之民猶有未輸租者，詔蠲之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, responsible officials reported that Hezhou had suffered disaster damage, and among people lacking food there were still some who had not paid rent; an edict remitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year, officials reported that Hezhou had been stricken by crop failure. Even among people already short of food, some remained in arrears on rent—so the throne ordered the levies remitted.

sentences.zh: 九月，以山東、河北三路被災，其權閣之租及借貸之粟，令俟歲豐日續征。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because the three circuits of Shandong and Hebei had suffered disaster, rent provisionally deferred and grain lent on loan were ordered to be collected only when harvests were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, because the three Shandong and Hebei circuits had been hit by disaster, deferred rent and loaned grain were to be collected only after a bumper harvest.

sentences.zh: 上如秋山，免圍場經過人戶今歲夏秋租稅之半。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Mount Qiu and remitted half of that year's summer and autumn rent and tax for households through which the hunting preserve passed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Mount Qiu for the autumn hunt, he remitted half the summer and autumn rent and tax for every household lying along the route of the imperial preserve.

sentences.zh: 四年冬十月，上行幸，諭旨尚書省曰：「海壖石城等縣，地瘠民困，所種惟黍稗而已。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the fourth year, the emperor traveled on tour and instructed the Ministry: "In counties such as Haichan and Shicheng, the land is barren and the people impoverished; what they plant is only broomcorn millet and barnyard millet.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the fourth year, on imperial tour, he instructed the Ministry: "In the coastal counties of Shicheng and elsewhere, the soil is poor and the people are hard pressed—they grow nothing but coarse millet and barnyard grass.

sentences.zh: 及賦於官，必以易粟輸之。

translations.literal: When levies are paid to the government, they must invariably be rendered by exchanging grain.
translations.idiomatic: When taxes come due, they must be paid in grain obtained by barter.

sentences.zh: 或令止課所產，或依河東路減稅，至還京當定議以聞。

translations.literal: Either order collection only of what is produced, or reduce taxes according to the Hedong Circuit precedent; when I return to the capital a decision shall be fixed and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Either assess only what the land actually yields, or reduce taxes along Hedong Circuit lines—I will decide on a definitive policy when I return to the capital and report it.

sentences.zh: 」五年，敕免河決被災之民秋租。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year, an order remitted autumn rent for people stricken by river-breach disaster.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year, an edict remitted the autumn rent of those stricken when the river broke its banks.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年四月，以久旱下詔責躬，免所旱州縣今年夏稅。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Taihe, because of prolonged drought an edict blaming himself was issued, remitting this year's summer tax for drought-stricken prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Taihe 4, after a prolonged drought the emperor issued a self-reproach edict and remitted the summer tax for every drought-stricken prefecture and county that year.

sentences.zh: 九月，陳言者謂：「河間、滄州逃戶，物力錢至數千貫，而其差發，有司止取辦於見戶，民不能堪矣！

translations.literal: In the ninth month, a memorialist said: "In Hejian and Cangzhou, absconding households owe wuli cash reaching several thousand strings, yet when corvée assignments are made, responsible officials satisfy them only from registered present households—the people cannot bear it!
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, a memorialist said: "In Hejian and Cangzhou, absconding households owe thousands of strings in wuli levies, yet when corvée is assigned officials squeeze only the households still on the rolls—the burden is unbearable!

sentences.zh: 」詔令按察司，除地土物力命隨其業，而權止其浮財物力。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the Intendant Offices: exempt land-based wuli linked to their occupations, and provisionally suspend their movable-property wuli.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered the Intendant Offices to exempt land-based wuli assessments tied to each household's occupation and temporarily suspend levies on movable property.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，詔有司：「自泰和三年嘗所行幸至三次者，被科之民特免半年租稅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, an edict to responsible officials said: "From the third year of Taihe, for places the emperor has toured on three occasions, the people assessed shall specially be remitted half a year's rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, the throne told responsible officials: "From Taihe 3 onward, wherever the emperor has toured three times, the districts levied for those visits shall receive a special half-year remission of rent and tax.

sentences.zh: 」八年五月，以宋謀和，詔天下，免河南、山東、陝西六路今年夏稅，河東、河北、大名等五路半之。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the eighth year, because Song sought peace, an edict to all under heaven remitted this year's summer tax for the six circuits of Henan, Shandong, and Shaanxi, and halved it for the five circuits of Hedong, Hebei, Daming, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month of the eighth year, with Song seeking peace, an edict throughout the realm remitted the summer tax for Henan, Shandong, and Shaanxi—six circuits in all—and cut it by half in Hedong, Hebei, Daming, and four other circuits.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔諸路農民請佃荒田者，與免租賦三年，作己業者一年，自首冒佃、及請佃黃河退灘地者，不在免例。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict said that farmers in all circuits who applied to cultivate wasteland received three years' remission of rent and levies; those who made it their own holding received one year; those who confessed to encroaching cultivation, and those who applied to cultivate Yellow River receded-bank land, were not within the exemption.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, farmers in every circuit who leased wasteland were granted three years free of rent and levies; those converting land to private holdings received one year. Encroachers who came forward, and anyone applying for newly exposed Yellow River flats, were excluded.

sentences.zh: 宣宗貞祐三年十月，禦史田迥秀言：「方今軍國所需，一切責之河南。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Zhenyou under Emperor Xuanzong, Censor Tian Jiongxiu said: "At present everything the army and state require is charged entirely to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhenyou 3, under Emperor Xuanzong, Censor Tian Jiongxiu said: "Everything the army and the state now need is loaded onto Henan alone.

sentences.zh: 有司不惜民力，徵調太急，促其期限，痛其棰楚。

translations.literal: Responsible officials do not spare the people's strength; requisitions and levies are too urgent, deadlines are pressed, and beatings are severe.
translations.idiomatic: Officials spare no civilian labor; levies come too fast, deadlines too tight, and the lash falls too hard.

sentences.zh: 民既罄其所有而不足，遂使奔走傍求於它境，力竭財殫，相踵散亡，禁之不能止也，乞自今凡科征必先期告之，不急者皆罷，庶民力寬而逋者可複。

translations.literal: Once the people had exhausted all they owned and still fell short, they were driven to run about seeking help in other regions; strength spent and wealth exhausted, they fled one after another, and prohibition could not stop it. He begged that from now on every levy be announced in advance, that none urgent be imposed, so that the people's strength might be eased and absconders might return.
translations.idiomatic: When people had spent everything and still could not meet the demands, they wandered into neighboring districts for help; exhausted and destitute, they fled in waves no prohibition could stop. He asked that every levy hereafter be announced well in advance, that non-urgent collections be canceled outright, so the people might breathe and absconders might come home.

sentences.zh: 」詔行之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered it implemented.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne ordered his proposal carried out.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔免逃戶租稅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict remitted rent and tax for absconding households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, an edict remitted the rent and taxes of absconding households.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，免陝西逃戶租。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, rent for absconding households in Shaanxi was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year, the rent of absconding households in Shaanxi was remitted.

sentences.zh: 五月，山東行省僕散安貞言：「泗州被災，道殣相望，所食者草根木皮而已。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Shandong Branch Secretariat Pusan Anzhen said: "Sizhou has suffered disaster; corpses lie along the roads, and what people eat is only tree roots and bark.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Pusan Anzhen of the Shandong Branch Secretariat reported: "Sizhou has been devastated. Corpses line the roads, and people survive on roots and bark.

sentences.zh: 而邳州戍兵數萬，急征重役，悉出三縣，官吏酷暴，擅括宿藏，以應一切之命。

translations.literal: Yet at Pizhou several tens of thousands of garrison troops urgently levied heavy corvée, all borne by three counties; officials were cruel and violent, arrogantly confiscating hidden stores to meet every command.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Pizhou's garrison of tens of thousands pressed urgent and heavy corvée, draining three counties dry. Officials were brutal, seizing hidden stores at will to satisfy every requisition.

sentences.zh: 民皆逋竄，又別遣進納閑官以相迫督。

translations.literal: The people all fled to escape obligations, and surplus collection officials were separately dispatched to press and supervise.
translations.idiomatic: The people fled in mass; idle surplus officials were sent out separately to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 皆怙勢營私，實到官者才十之一，而徒使國家有厚斂之名。

translations.literal: All relied on power to pursue private gain; what actually reached government was only one in ten, yet the state gained nothing but a reputation for heavy exaction.
translations.idiomatic: They abused their authority for private profit—barely a tenth of what was collected ever reached the treasury—while the state earned only a name for rapacious taxation.

sentences.zh: 乞命信臣革此弊以安百姓。

translations.literal: He begged that trusted ministers be ordered to reform this abuse and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that trustworthy officials be dispatched to end these abuses and restore order among the people.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 興定元年二月，免中京、嵩、汝等逋租十六萬石。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xingding, 160,000 shi of unpaid rent from Zhongjing, Song, Ru, and the like was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xingding 1, 160,000 shi of arrears in Zhongjing, Song, Ru, and neighboring districts were remitted.

sentences.zh: 四年，禦史中丞完顏伯嘉奏：「亳州大水，計當免租三十萬石，而三司官不以實報，止免十萬而已。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Censor-in-Chief Wanyan Bojia memorialized: "In Bozhou great flood struck; the calculation should have remitted three hundred thousand shi of rent, yet Three Departments officials did not report truthfully and remitted only one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Censor-in-Chief Wanyan Bojia memorialized: "Bozhou suffered severe flooding—a full remission should have amounted to 300,000 shi of rent, but Three Departments officials underreported the figure and remitted only 100,000.

sentences.zh: 」詔命治三司官虛妄之罪。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered punishment of the Three Departments officials for false reporting.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered the false-reporting Three Departments officials punished.

sentences.zh: 七月，以河南大水，下詔免租勸種，且命參知政事李複亨為宣慰使，中丞完顏伯嘉副之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, because of great flood in Henan, an edict remitted rent and encouraged planting, and appointed Vice Grand Councillor Li Fuheng as Pacification Commissioner, with Censor-in-Chief Wanyan Bojia as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, after catastrophic flooding in Henan, an edict remitted rent and urged replanting. Vice Grand Councillor Li Fuheng was named Pacification Commissioner, with Censor-in-Chief Wanyan Bojia as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 十月，以久雨，令寬民輸稅之限。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, because of prolonged rain, the deadline for people to deliver taxes was relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, prolonged rains brought an extension of the tax-payment deadline.

sentences.zh: 十一月，上曰：「聞百姓多逃，而逋賦皆抑配見戶，人何以堪？

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the emperor said: "I hear that many common people have fled, yet unpaid levies are all forcibly apportioned to registered present households—how can people bear it?
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the emperor said: "I hear that commoners are fleeing in numbers, yet unpaid levies are forced onto the households still on the rolls—how can anyone endure it?

sentences.zh: 軍儲既足，宜悉除免。

translations.literal: Since military stores are already sufficient, all should be completely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: With military stores already full, these levies should be remitted outright.

sentences.zh: 今又添軍須錢太多，亡者詎肯複業乎？

translations.literal: Now military-supply cash is added in too great amount—will those who have fled be willing to return to their occupations?
translations.idiomatic: And now military-supply levies are piled on top—why would anyone who has fled ever come home?

sentences.zh: 」遂命行部官閱實免之，已代納者給以恩例，或除它役，仍減桑皮故紙錢四之一。

translations.literal: " He then ordered touring officials to verify and remit them; those who had already paid on others' behalf were granted favors, or exempted from other corvée, and the mulberry-bark and waste-paper fee was reduced by one quarter.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered touring officials to verify the accounts and grant remissions. Those who had already paid arrears for others were rewarded with favors or exempted from other corvée, and the mulberry-bark and waste-paper levy was cut by one quarter.

sentences.zh: 三年，令逃戶複業者但輸本租，余差役一切皆免。

translations.literal: In the third year, absconding households returning to their occupations were ordered to pay only basic rent; all other corvée and levies were entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, absconders who returned to farming owed only their basic rent; all other corvée and special levies were waived.

sentences.zh: 能代耕者，免如複戶。

translations.literal: Those able to substitute-plow received the same remissions as returning households.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could farm on behalf of absconders received the same exemptions as returning households.

sentences.zh: 有司失信擅科者，以違制論。

translations.literal: Responsible officials who broke faith and levied on their own authority were punished under the statute for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who broke faith and levied without authorization were prosecuted for violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，鎮南軍節度使溫蒂罕思敬上書言：「今民輸稅，其法大抵有三，上戶輸遠倉，中戶次之，下戶最近。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Zhennan Army Military Commissioner Wendihan Sijing submitted a memorial saying: "At present when the people deliver taxes, the method falls broadly into three grades: upper households deliver to distant granaries, middle households next, and lower households to the nearest.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Zhennan Army Military Commissioner Wendihan Sijing wrote: "When people deliver taxes today, the rule divides households into three grades: upper households haul to distant granaries, middle households to middling ones, lower households to the nearest.

sentences.zh: 然近者不下百里，遠者數百里，道路之費倍於所輸，而雨雪有稽違之責。

translations.literal: Yet even the nearest is no less than one hundred li, and the farthest several hundred li; road costs double what is delivered, and rain or snow brings liability for delay violations.
translations.idiomatic: Even the nearest granary lies a hundred li away and the farthest several hundred; transport costs can double the tax itself, and rain or snow bring penalties for late delivery.

sentences.zh: 遇賊有死傷之患。

translations.literal: Meeting bandits brings risk of death and injury.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits along the road bring risk of death.

sentences.zh: 不若止輸本郡，令有司檢算倉之所積，稱屯兵之數，使就食之。

translations.literal: Better to deliver only within the native commandery, let responsible officials inspect and calculate granary stores and match the number of garrison troops, and have them consume locally.
translations.idiomatic: Better to pay taxes locally: let officials tally each granary's stores against local garrison strength and feed the troops on the spot.

sentences.zh: 若有不足，則增斂於民，民計所斂不及道裏之費，將忻然從之矣！

translations.literal: If there is shortfall, then increase collection from the people—the people, calculating that what is levied falls short of road-mileage costs, will gladly comply!
translations.idiomatic: If stores still fall short, levy a surcharge—but when people find the surcharge cheaper than haulage, they will gladly pay it!

sentences.zh: 」五年十月，上諭宰臣曰：「比欲民多種麥，故令所在官貸易麥種。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month of the fifth year, the emperor told the chief ministers: "Recently, wishing the people to plant more wheat, I ordered local officials to lend and exchange wheat seed.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month of the fifth year, the emperor told his chief ministers: "I wanted farmers to grow more wheat, so I ordered local offices to lend seed on exchange terms.

sentences.zh: 今聞實不貸與，而虛立案簿，反收其數以補不足之租。

translations.literal: Now I hear they in fact do not lend it, but falsely create register accounts, and instead collect the amount to make up shortfalls in rent.
translations.idiomatic: I now hear they never lend the seed at all—they keep hollow ledger entries and simply collect the nominal amounts to cover rent shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 其遣使究治。」

translations.literal: Have envoys sent to investigate and punish."
translations.idiomatic: Send investigators and punish the offenders."

sentences.zh: 牛頭稅

translations.literal: Ox-head tax
translations.idiomatic: Tax on Ox Teams

sentences.zh: 即牛具稅，猛安謀克部女直戶所輸之稅也。

translations.literal: That is, the ox-team tax—the tax paid by Jurchen households in meng'an-mouke units.
translations.idiomatic: This was the ox-team tax paid by Jurchen households registered in meng'an-mouke units.

sentences.zh: 其制每耒牛三頭為一具，限民口二十五受田四頃四畝有奇，歲輸粟大約不過一石，官民占田無過四十具。

translations.literal: Under the system, every three plow oxen constituted one team; per twenty-five registered mouths, land received was four qing and four mu plus a fraction; annual grain delivered generally did not exceed one shi; government and commoner holdings in land did not exceed forty teams.
translations.idiomatic: The rule fixed three draft oxen as one team. A household of twenty-five mouths received just over four qing of land and owed at most one shi of grain yearly. No meng'an household, official or civilian, could hold more than forty teams.

sentences.zh: 天會三年，太宗以歲稔，官無儲積無以備饑謹，詔令一耒賦粟一石，每謀克別為一廩貯之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhui, Emperor Taizong, because the year was abundant yet government had no stored reserves to guard against famine, ordered one plow ox taxed one shi of grain, with each mouke separately maintaining a granary for storage.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 3, after a bumper harvest left the state with no reserves against famine, Emperor Taizong ordered one shi of grain per plow ox. Each mouke was to maintain its own granary.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔內地諸路，每牛一具賦粟五斗，為定制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict to the various circuits of the interior fixed the levy at five dou of grain per ox team as permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, interior circuits were ordered to fix the levy at five dou per ox team as standing law.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定元年，詔諸猛安不經遷移者，征牛具稅粟，就命謀克監其倉，虧損則坐之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, an edict said that meng'an units not subject to relocation should have ox-team grain tax collected, with mouke immediately ordered to supervise the granaries; shortfalls were prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 1, Emperor Shizong ordered unmoved meng'an units to pay the ox-team grain tax, with each mouke supervising its granary; losses were punishable.

sentences.zh: 十二年，尚書省奏：「唐古部民舊同猛安謀克定稅，其後改同州縣，履畝立稅，頗以為重。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Ministry memorialized: "Tanggou tribesmen formerly had taxes fixed like meng'an-mouke; afterward they were changed to the same as prefectures and counties, with tax assessed by the mu—a burden widely regarded as heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the Ministry reported: "Tanggou tribesmen once paid taxes under meng'an-mouke rules; after they were treated like county households and taxed per mu, the burden was widely felt as crushing.

sentences.zh: 」遂命從舊制。

translations.literal: " They were then ordered to follow the old system.
translations.idiomatic: " They were ordered back to the old system.

sentences.zh: 二十年，定功授世襲謀克，許以親族從行，當給以地者，除牛九具以下全給，十具以上四十具以下者，則於官豪之家量撥地六具與之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, for meritorious awards of hereditary mouke rank, kin permitted to accompany them, and land to be granted: below nine ox teams all was granted in full; from ten teams up to forty, six teams' worth of land was apportioned from official and powerful households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when meritorious service earned hereditary mouke rank and kin were permitted to follow, land grants were fixed: households owed fewer than nine ox teams received full allotments; those rated ten to forty teams received land equivalent to six teams, reassigned from official and wealthy estates.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，世宗謂宰臣曰：「前時一歲所收可支三年，比聞今歲山西豐稔，所獲可支三年。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Shizong told the chief ministers: "Formerly one year's collection could supply three years; recently I hear that this year Shanxi had a bountiful harvest and the yield can supply three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, Shizong told his ministers: "Once a year's harvest could feed the realm for three. I hear Shanxi is having a bumper year—enough, they say, for three years' supply.

sentences.zh: 此間地一歲所獲不能支半歲，而又牛頭稅粟，每牛一頭止令各輸三斗，又多逋懸，此皆遞互隱匿所致，當令盡實輸之。

translations.literal: In this region one year's yield cannot supply half a year; moreover ox-head grain tax, though each ox is ordered to pay only three dou, has much unpaid arrears—all caused by mutual concealment. They should be made to pay in full according to reality.
translations.idiomatic: Here one harvest barely lasts six months. For the ox-head grain tax, each ox owes only three dou—yet arrears mount, all from hidden evasion. Make them pay every bit owed.

sentences.zh: 」二十三年，有司奏其事，世宗謂左丞完顏襄曰：「卿家舊止七具，今定為四十具，朕始令卿等議此，而卿皆不欲，蓋各顧其私爾。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-third year, responsible officials memorialized the matter. Shizong said to Left Vice Grand Councillor Wanyan Xiang: "Your household formerly had only seven teams; now it is fixed at forty. I first had you discuss this, yet none of you wished it—you only looked after your private interests.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twenty-third year, when officials memorialized on the matter, Shizong said to Left Vice Grand Councillor Wanyan Xiang: "Your clan once held seven ox teams; now the register lists forty. I asked you ministers to debate this—you refused, each protecting his own interest.

sentences.zh: 是後限民口二十五，算牛一具。

translations.literal: After this, per twenty-five registered mouths one ox team was calculated.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter one ox team was tallied for every twenty-five mouths.

sentences.zh: 」七月，尚書省複奏其事，上慮版籍歲久貧富不同，猛安謀克又皆年少，不練時事，一旦軍興，按籍征之必有不均之患。

translations.literal: " In the seventh month, the Ministry again memorialized the matter. The emperor feared that after registers had aged long, rich and poor differed, and meng'an-mouke were all young and inexperienced in affairs; once war arose, levying by register would surely bring unevenness.
translations.idiomatic: " In the seventh month the Ministry raised the issue again. The emperor feared that after decades on the rolls, wealth no longer matched the records—and with young, inexperienced meng'an-mouke in charge, a war mobilization keyed to old registers would land unevenly on the people.

sentences.zh: 乃令驗實推排。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered verified reassessment survey.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a verified household reassessment.

sentences.zh: 閱其戶口、畜產之數，其以上京二十二路來上。

translations.literal: Their household registers and livestock holdings were reviewed, and results were submitted from the twenty-two circuits above Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers and livestock were audited; returns came in from the twenty-two circuits north of Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 八月，尚書省奏，推排定猛安謀克戶口、田畝、牛具之數。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Ministry memorialized that the reassessment had fixed the numbers of meng'an-mouke households, field mu, and ox teams.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Ministry reported the reassessment totals for meng'an-mouke households, field acreage, and ox teams.

sentences.zh: 猛安二百二，謀克千八百七十八，戶六十一萬五千六百二十四，口六百一十五萬八千六百三十六，內正口四百八十一萬二千六百六十九，奴婢口一百三十四萬五千九百六十七，田一百六十九萬三百八十頃有奇，牛具三十八萬四千七百七十一。

translations.literal: Meng'an 202, mouke 1,878, households 615,624, mouths 6,158,636, including registered mouths 4,812,669, servile mouths 1,345,967, fields 1,690,380 qing plus a fraction, ox teams 384,771.
translations.idiomatic: The count: 202 meng'an, 1,878 mouke, 615,624 households, 6,158,636 mouths (4,812,669 registered, 1,345,967 servile), 1,690,380-plus qing of land, and 384,771 ox teams.

sentences.zh: 在都宗室將軍司，戶一百七十，口二萬八千七百九十，內正口九百八十二，奴婢口二萬七千八百八，田三千六百八十三頃七十五畝有奇，牛具三百四。

translations.literal: For the Metropolitan Imperial-Clan General's Office: households 170, mouths 28,790, including registered mouths 982, servile mouths 27,808, fields 3,683 qing 75 mu plus a fraction, ox teams 304.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital's Imperial-Clan General's Office: 170 households, 28,790 mouths (982 registered, 27,808 servile), 3,683 qing 75 mu plus a fraction of land, and 304 ox teams.

sentences.zh: 迭剌、唐古二部五颭，戶五千五百八十五，口一十三萬七千五百四十四，內正口十一萬九千四百六十三，奴婢口一萬八千八十一，田四萬六千二十四頃一十七畝，牛具五千六十六。

translations.literal: For the Diela and Tanggou two divisions, five banners: households 5,585, mouths 137,544, including registered mouths 119,463, servile mouths 18,081, fields 46,024 qing 17 mu, ox teams 5,066.
translations.idiomatic: For the Diela and Tanggou divisions across five banners: 5,585 households, 137,544 mouths (119,463 registered, 18,081 servile), 46,024 qing 17 mu of land, and 5,066 ox teams.

sentences.zh: 後二十六年，尚書省奏並征牛頭稅粟，上曰：「積壓五年，一見並征，民何以堪？

translations.literal: Twenty-six years later, the Ministry memorialized collecting ox-head grain tax in a lump sum. The emperor said: "Accumulated over five years—a single lump collection—how can the people bear it?
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-six years later, when the Ministry proposed collecting five years of ox-head grain tax at once, the emperor said: "Five years piled into one levy—how can the people endure it?

sentences.zh: 其令民隨年輸納。

translations.literal: Order the people to pay year by year.
translations.idiomatic: Let the people pay year by year.

sentences.zh: 被災者蠲之，貸者俟豐年征還。」

translations.literal: Those stricken by disaster shall be remitted; loans shall be collected when harvests are abundant."
translations.idiomatic: Remit levies where disaster strikes; collect loans only in bumper years."
